Thanks again for the demo this morning, Logan — helpful session.

Short version of what we need from Redwood to take this to procurement: a clear recommendation on Dedicated vs Hosted for our use case, a realistic sizing estimate (GPU class, expected TPS, concurrency), and any constraints around token retention/KV caching for our product.

A few specifics from our end:
- Peak queries: ~3,000 qps across the US (spiky; 60% of traffic during business hours).
- Typical prompt size: ~280 tokens in, ~320 tokens out (average 600 tokens per request).
- Mix: ~70% standard generation (single-turn), 30% multi-turn chat sessions with KV cache reuse.
- SLA ask: 99.9% availability, 95th percentile latency target ~250ms for standard prompts.

Can you and the team align on a recommended Dedicated footprint (GPU family + count), expected sustained TPS assumptions, and whether a Private VPC is necessary given our data residency/privacy SLAs? Also appreciate a simple cost delta against Hosted for a rough procurement figure.

Thanks — Lydia

Lydia — thanks for the clear summary and the traffic breakdown. Quick recap + items we’ll deliver by EOD Tuesday:

1) Deployment recommendation: Dedicated capacity is the leading option given your sustained peak (3k qps) and the KV/cache sensitivity from multi-turn sessions. Hosted could work for initial experiments but won’t hit predictable latency or unit-cost targets at scale. If procurement insists on private control for compliance, we can map the same Dedicated configuration to a Private VPC deployment (adds network/ops steps).

2) Sizing (initial recommendation):
- GPU family: A100 80GB (or equivalent 80GB L40x under availability).
- Node count: 12 nodes with model sharding + balanced routing; this targets ~3k qps with headroom for bursts (assuming batching optimizations and prefix caching).
- Expected throughput: ~80-100 requests/sec per GPU node (subject to token mix and batching).
- Concurrency: plan for 40 concurrent in-flight streams per node; autoscaling/burst policy for +25% during peaks.

3) Token/cache notes:
- KV cache reuse for multi-turn sessions will significantly improve per-token latency and cost; we recommend enabling session affinity for chat flows and a TTL of 30 minutes for hot sessions.
- By default we keep transient KV in GPU-associated caching (not persisted) unless you opt into encrypted cache persistence in VPC.

4) Cost delta: Dedicated (reserved) is ~35–45% cheaper per-token vs Hosted at your scale — final number depends on commitment term and GPU pricing. Will give a back-of-envelope in the workbook.

Next steps: Marissa will attach a capacity workbook (workload assumptions + cost sketch) and Aditya will validate the 12-node A100 baseline with the infra team and propose an L40x fallback if A100 stock is constrained.

Can you confirm the 600-token average assumption and whether the 3k qps peak is a sustained hour or a 5–10 minute spike? That affects node count.

Best,
Logan
